skill.name: etetoolkit
skill.description: Phylogenetic tree toolkit (ETE). Tree manipulation (Newick/NHX), evolutionary event detection, orthology/paralogy, NCBI taxonomy, visualization (PDF/SVG), for phylogenomics.
skill.summary: Guide ETE phylogenetic tree analysis, taxonomy lookup, orthology workflows, and tree visualization.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, ETE examples, and biological taxonomy lookups. Confirmed issues are the documented sudo package installation commands and the automatic NCBI taxonomy cache under the user home directory.

remediation.issue: Privileged system package installation is documented in SKILL.md.
remediation.suggestion: Replace sudo apt-get examples with manual setup guidance and require explicit user confirmation before any privileged installation.

remediation.issue: NCBITaxa may create ~/.etetoolkit/taxa.sqlite on first use.
remediation.suggestion: Document the download clearly, ask for consent before initialization, and prefer a configurable project-local database path when possible.

remediation.issue: Shell examples may be executed too broadly by automated agents.
remediation.suggestion: Mark command blocks as examples, separate read-only analysis from environment setup, and avoid automatic package installation.

content.value_statement: Phylogenetic tree analysis often requires many ETE APIs and file formats. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused workflows for tree editing, taxonomy lookup, orthology analysis, and visualization.
actual_capabilities: Explains ETE Tree, PhyloTree, ClusterTree, and NCBITaxa APIs with local reference files.
Shows how to read, write, convert, reroot, prune, and compare Newick trees.
Provides helper scripts for tree statistics, format conversion, rerooting, pruning, leaf listing, and ASCII views.
Guides NCBI taxid and name translation, lineage retrieval, taxonomy tree building, and tree annotation.
Describes orthology, paralogy, duplication, and speciation workflows for gene trees.
Provides visualization patterns for PDF, SVG, and PNG rendering with ETE styles and faces.
limitations: Requires the ete3 Python package and optional Qt dependencies for rendering or GUI features.
NCBITaxa may download a large local taxonomy database on first use.
Examples assume valid biological tree files and species names supplied by the user.
Does not provide a complete phylogenetic inference engine or sequence alignment tool.

use_cases.title: Prepare Gene Trees
use_cases.description: Clean, reroot, prune, and inspect Newick gene trees before downstream phylogenomic analysis.

use_cases.title: Automate Tree Processing
use_cases.description: Use helper scripts and workflow patterns to convert formats, list leaves, and batch process tree files.

use_cases.title: Create Publication Figures
use_cases.description: Render styled phylogenetic trees as PDF, SVG, or PNG with support values and custom layouts.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Tree
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the ETE Toolkit skill to inspect my Newick tree, explain the number of leaves, and suggest the right ETE format option.

prompt_templates.title: Convert and Reroot
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scripts/tree_operations.py to convert my Newick file to format 1, midpoint root it, and describe the output files I should expect.

prompt_templates.title: Annotate with Taxonomy
prompt_templates.prompt: Use NCBITaxa guidance to map these species names to taxids, build a minimal species tree, and note any ambiguous names.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Orthology Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an ETE PhyloTree workflow that loads a gene tree, extracts species names, detects duplication events, and saves ortholog group trees.

output_examples.input: User provides a Newick file and asks for preprocessing.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan to validate the tree, run statistics, midpoint root it, prune selected taxa, and save a clean Newick file.

output_examples.input: User asks for NCBI taxonomy annotation.
output_examples.output: A workflow that maps species names to taxids, retrieves lineages, annotates leaves, and warns about the first-run taxonomy cache.

output_examples.input: User needs a figure for publication.
output_examples.output: Rendering guidance for PDF or SVG output, support-value styling, circular layout options, and dependency notes for Qt.

best_practices: Use project-local input and output paths, and review generated files before overwriting existing trees.
Confirm NCBI taxonomy downloads and cache locations before running NCBITaxa in an automated agent.
Use SVG or PDF for publication figures, and keep PNG for raster previews.
anti_patterns: Do not run sudo package installation from an agent without explicit user approval.
Do not assume every leaf name contains a valid species token; define a clear parser.
Do not process very large trees with list-heavy traversal when iterators are available.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use ETE for phylogenetic tree analysis and visualization.

faq.question: Does it include runnable scripts?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes helper scripts for tree operations and quick visualization of Newick trees.

faq.question: Can it infer new phylogenetic trees?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on manipulating, annotating, comparing, and visualizing trees that already exist.

faq.question: Does it use NCBI taxonomy data?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation explains NCBITaxa workflows for taxid translation, lineage retrieval, and taxonomy trees.

faq.question: Why are Qt dependencies mentioned?
faq.answer: ETE rendering and GUI features may need Qt packages, especially when exporting figures or using interactive views.

faq.question: Is this safe for automated agents?
faq.answer: Use caution. The skill documents sudo package installation and a first-run taxonomy database download.
